bull.b: TTM operating cash flow of roughly $509M and free cash flow of approximately $463M show that reported earnings are converting into liquidity. This internally generated cash can fund brand support, manufacturing expansion and shareholder returns, giving Celsius resilience during portfolio integration and operating volatility.

A roughly 20% U.S. energy-drink dollar share demonstrates meaningful market position, while higher dollars per distribution point indicates productive retail placement. This scale can improve retailer access, support execution leverage and strengthen sell-through as Celsius develops its multi-brand platform.

bull.t: Alani Nu Growth and Brand Diversification
bull.b: Alani Nu's rapid sales growth adds a substantial second growth engine beyond the core CELSIUS brand. Its strong tracked-channel performance and limited-time-offer momentum broaden the portfolio, diversify revenue sources and provide a platform for continued multi-brand expansion.

bear.b: The sharp increase in debt-to-equity materially reduces financial flexibility compared with prior years. Although Celsius continues to generate substantial cash, higher leverage raises the importance of maintaining earnings and cash flow, while leaving less balance-sheet capacity if margins or demand weaken.

Net margin compression shows that rapid revenue growth has not translated into equally durable profit expansion. Persistent aluminum, diesel and freight pressures, together with promotional investment, can limit operating leverage and constrain the cash available for reinvestment if costs remain elevated.

bear.t: Core CELSIUS Sales and Execution Weakness
bear.b: The core CELSIUS brand is facing a meaningful sales decline while SKU rationalization, inventory rebalancing and distribution changes continue. Management expects another similar quarter, so near-term execution pressure may persist and delay the return to growth despite planned innovation and recovery initiatives.
